Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2216); Zorobabel (i.e. Zerubbabel), an Israelite:--Zorobabel.
BiblicalUsage: Zorobabel is the Greek form of Zerubbabel, the governor who led the first exiles home and laid the foundation of the second temple. Matthew names him in the genealogy of Jesus, son of Shealtiel and father of Abiud; Luke names him in the genealogy too, son of Shealtiel by another line. Two genealogies, one man, and the line runs straight through him to Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Zerubbabel matters because the promise kept moving through him — the exiles came home, the temple rose again, and the line of David did not break.
